purpose: Twenty individual community/government starting guides with useful selected source paths and honestly scoped credited pictures, not twenty exhaustive histories or distinct-nation counts.
sourceStandard: No fixed source minimum. Original source-review scopes/dates are preserved; supporting context is excluded from substantive-work counts.

profiles.name: Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas
remainingGaps: Compare the community narrative with original agreements and fuller local histories.
Current legal provisions, officeholders and program outcomes need separate dated review.
Broaden named community voices; no community endorsement is recorded.

profiles.name: Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas
remainingGaps: Compare later government instruments and cross-border histories with the1983 enactment.
Read more Texas community-authored and family accounts without conflating Mexican, Kansas or Oklahoma communities.
Present program delivery, language outcomes and individual legal questions remain unassessed.

profiles.name: Texas Band of Yaqui Indians
remainingGaps: Corroborate particular Texas migration and family-history accounts through accessible original records.
Review governing and recognition claims separately rather than inferring legal consequences from a name or commemorative resolution.
Broaden independently inspected community voices and evaluate program history without claiming measured outcomes.

profiles.name: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes
remainingGaps: Read the governing instrument and newer institutional records before describing current rules.
Add more community-authored family and place histories with appropriate access limits.
Underlying archives, recordings, program outcomes and individual citizenship questions are not reviewed.

profiles.name: Coeur d'Alene Tribe
remainingGaps: Compare selected community chronology with dated agreements and land records; current legal rules are not established.
Update environmental implementation through newer records before describing present cleanup conditions.
Broaden family, arts and foodways voices; no community review or language-outcomes assessment is recorded.

profiles.name: Kootenai Tribe of Idaho
remainingGaps: Compare the community history with underlying treaty and administrative records.
Check later constitutional amendments before describing present law or citizenship.
Add community voices and independent ecological evaluation; program aspirations are not verified recovery outcomes.

profiles.name: Nez Perce Tribe
remainingGaps: Compare the historical narrative with original treaties, allotment records and specific case holdings.
Broaden family, language, artistic and foodways voices; this institutional selection is not comprehensive.

profiles.name: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation
remainingGaps: Compare treaty promises, relocation chronology and later land reductions with underlying records.
Review current constitutional amendments and program access before making present legal or service claims.

profiles.name: Shoshone-Paiute Tribes
remainingGaps: Compare the public history with original executive orders and broader community voices.
Review original constitutional scans, later amendments and current tribal law before making legal claims.

profiles.name: Bois Forte Band of Chippewa
remainingGaps: Read selected public Bois Forte oral-history transcripts with speaker, date and consent/publication context; only the interview index was previously inspected.
Compare the cited treaty chronology and 1881 executive order with the actual instruments and place-specific historical scholarship.
Add community-authored language learning material and a dated account of present program outcomes.

profiles.name: Fond du Lac Band of Lake Superior Chippewa
remainingGaps: Add a direct Band public-history account and inspect primary treaty records; this starting profile concentrates on language and food sovereignty.
Inspect selected public language lessons or videos and identify their teachers, intended audience and reuse terms.
Check current Gitigaaning and language-program operations through dated community publications.
The selected photograph supplies explicitly labeled regional watershed context; an exact Band institution or reservation landscape image with reusable rights remains desirable.

profiles.name: Grand Portage Band of Lake Superior Chippewa
remainingGaps: Add a longer community-authored history and public Ojibwemowin material.
Inspect the actual treaty and parcel title/allotment records before expanding the 2026 release into a legal land history.
The selected photograph dates to 1984 and shows a reconstructed public site; present appearance and visitor information were not audited.

profiles.name: Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe
remainingGaps: Compare the historical overview with primary treaties, dated court opinions and the cited archival records.
Inspect the actual 2019 MOU and later implementation materials separately, then check current co-management arrangements.
Add public community language and everyday-life accounts beyond this institutional resource-management publication.

profiles.name: Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe
remainingGaps: Inspect the actual 1837 and 1855 treaties and reported judicial opinions before expanding legal conclusions.
Read the linked Social History and additional pages of the Non-Removable Guide as separate, explicitly scoped tasks.
Add direct public language resources, named community voices and a dated account of present priorities.

profiles.name: Red Lake Nation
remainingGaps: Read primary treaty and land-agreement texts and compare the timeline’s allotment terminology, chronology and acreage claims.
Add constitutional documents and a dated contemporary government publication.
Add public Red Lake language resources and named community historical voices; the linked historical-photo video was not reviewed.

profiles.name: White Earth Nation
remainingGaps: Compare reservation history with original instruments and wider community voices.

Current language fluency, program access and community review remain unverified.
